name: strr (UPGo McGill)
what_it_holds: R package (from David Wachsmuth's UPGo Lab at McGill, the group behind the Airbnb-and-the-rent-gap / gentrification literature adjacent to this theme) providing functions to clean/compress/expand raw AirDNA property and daily files, detect multi-listing commercial operators (strr_multi), frequently-rented entire-home listings (strr_FREH), 'ghost hostel' clusters of private rooms in one building (strr_ghost), classify listings as real housing units (strr_housing), and estimate true listing locations from fuzzy map pins (strr_raffle). No large datasets committed; this is a processing/analysis toolkit meant to be pointed at AirDNA or Inside-Airbnb-shaped inputs. Actively developed (400+ commits).
why_useful: A maintained, published toolkit for exactly the realised-occupancy/commercial-operator questions in gap #2 (AirDNA-style exports) and for classifying professional vs. casual hosts — useful if the team ever obtains an AirDNA sample or Inside Airbnb calendar data and wants a vetted commercial-listing / ghost-hostel detector rather than building one from scratch; academically used by McGill's Urban Politics and Governance lab in several STR housing-impact papers, including work touching NYC-style regulation questions.
geography: generic (used in Montreal, Toronto, Los Angeles, New York studies by the same lab)
time_coverage: N/A (processing toolkit, not a stored dataset)
themes: Inside Airbnb New York City snapshots around Local Law 18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) stored in repos

name: idealista18
what_it_holds: Committed open real-estate-listing dataset scraped from Idealista.com for three major Spanish cities (Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia) for the year 2018, published as a companion to a peer-reviewed paper (DOI 10.1177/23998083241242844). Includes for-sale and likely rental listing records with price, location, size fields under ODbL-1.0 licence.
why_useful: Long-term-rental pricing panel for major EU cities (2018 vintage) is a real, licensed-for-reuse, committed dataset — directly fills gap #13 (LTR data for STR↔LTR crossover / host supply economics) and is old enough to be a useful historical anchor Inside Airbnb itself lacks.
size_hint: city-level listings dataset, exact row count not confirmed from search metadata; academic paper companion
themes: Rental listing scrapers and datasets (Craigslist, Zillow rentals, Apartments.com, Idealista, Rightmove, Zoopla, Immoscout24, SeLoger, Immobiliare, Domain, realestate.com.au)
why_all: Long-term-rental pricing panel for major EU cities (2018 vintage) is a real, licensed-for-reuse, committed dataset — directly fills gap #13 (LTR data for STR↔LTR crossover / host supply economics) and is old enough to be a useful historical anchor Inside Airbnb itself lacks.

name: fitnr/acris-download
what_it_holds: Python tool + SQL schema (mysql.sql, postgres.sql, sqlite.sql) that downloads NYC's ACRIS real-estate transaction records (deeds, mortgages, liens, party names/entities on every recorded document) from the NYC Open Data portal and loads them into a database. No data files committed, but the schema is ready-made for parsing entity/LLC names on deed and mortgage documents. 69 stars, updated 30 Jul 2026 (active).
why_useful: Directly targets gap 13 (housing supply/LLC ownership) and the theme's ACRIS ask: ACRIS party names are the standard way to identify LLC-shell buyers of NYC real estate, a proxy for investor purchase activity and STR-conversion housing supply in the largest ABNB market for domestic urban nights.
size_hint: code + SQL schema only, no committed data rows; pulls from full ACRIS history (1966-present) via NYC Open Data API
themes: Housing supply and investor activity: building permits, Redfin investor purchases, mortgage rates, county assessor/parcel data, LLC ownership, NYC PLUTO/ACRIS
why_all: Directly targets gap 13 (housing supply/LLC ownership) and the theme's ACRIS ask: ACRIS party names are the standard way to identify LLC-shell buyers of NYC real estate, a proxy for investor purchase activity and STR-conversion housing supply in the largest ABNB market for domestic urban nights.

name: who-owns-what (JustFix.nyc)
what_it_holds: Django/PostgreSQL + React app and backend SQL functions that map NYC landlord portfolios and shell-company/LLC ownership networks using HPD Registration (~160k properties), PLUTO, and ACRIS deed/ownership records; identifies buildings a given owner network controls and flags financially distressed buildings. 1,172 commits, GPLv3, ~39 open issues, ongoing maintenance.
why_useful: Purpose-built LLC-ownership-network tool over NYC PLUTO/ACRIS/HPD data -- exactly the 'LLC ownership' and 'NYC PLUTO/ACRIS' items named in the theme; usable to identify institutional/investor-controlled rental portfolios in NYC as a host-supply-concentration proxy (gap 13).
time_coverage: HPD registrations current + historical filings, ongoing
themes: Housing supply and investor activity: building permits, Redfin investor purchases, mortgage rates, county assessor/parcel data, LLC ownership, NYC PLUTO/ACRIS

name: digital-nomad-visa-data (GlobeNomad Visa Dataset)
what_it_holds: data/visas.json: 53 digital-nomad-visa programmes across 46 countries (Thailand alone has 4 pathways), one record per programme with fields documented in SCHEMA.md; CHANGELOG.md shows a schema restructure 2026-08-27 (one row per programme instead of per country); each record cites an official government source page and a verification timestamp. CC-BY-4.0. Small (~single JSON file) but structured and maintained.
why_useful: Directly fills gap #16 (digital-nomad visa datasets) with a maintained, sourced, timestamped panel of nomad-visa program existence/terms across 46 countries — usable as a proxy for long-stay/remote-work demand geography that could interact with ABNB's long-stay mix and regional nights growth (LatAm/APAC visa launches).
time_coverage: live/current snapshot, versioned via CHANGELOG since at least 2026; not a historical time series
themes: Coliving, corporate housing, furnished mid-term rental data (Blueground, Landing, Furnished Finder, Zeus), remote-work and digital-nomad data (WFH Research SWAA, Nomad List, nomad visas)
wildcard: a computational social scientist who works with Reddit dumps
why_all: Directly fills gap #16 (digital-nomad visa datasets) with a maintained, sourced, timestamped panel of nomad-visa program existence/terms across 46 countries — usable as a proxy for long-stay/remote-work demand geography that could interact with ABNB's long-stay mix and regional nights growth (LatAm/APAC visa launches).
